TARGET COMMERCIAL APPLICATION Direct air capture utilization and storage (DAC-US) is a complementary technology to point-source carbon capture utilization and storage (CCUS) and vital to meet CO mitigation targets of 1.5°C scenario. DAC- 2 US captures CO from ambient air and subsequently converts it to a salable productor or stores the CO to 2 2 prevent it from being released back into the atmosphere. Extensive deployment of DAC can mitigate Technology Maturation Plan 7 Susteon Inc. DE-FE0032254 distributed CO emissions from industries such as transportation and aviation. Beyond negative emissions, 2 DAC units can be placed ubiquitously to capture and utilize CO for a wide variety of applications. 2 Installing DAC at the sequestration hub's vicinity can reduce transport and storage costs by eliminating expensive pipelines. Expanding DAC deployment on a large scale unlocks significant potential to convert CO to high-value products while reducing CO emission levels. Some of the CO utilization pathways that 2 2 2 have been integrated to point-source CO capture can be integrated downstream of the DAC unit. Successful 2 examples of such integrations are converting CO into methanol and acetic acid or fixing CO in building 2 2 block materials. These advantages of DAC technologies become a strong promoter for the commercial deployment of these systems. Most DAC technologies are modular, which extends the prospect of more rapid scaling by numbering them up. The regeneration of Susteon’s DAC sorbent can be done with direct electric heating, enabling the use of renewable power such as solar PV and wind. The use of direct electric heating of the EcoFilters for CO desorption results in rapid ramping of the DAC system, in the order of minutes, and a 2 high turndown ratio. This allows the system to operate around the variable availability of renewable energy. 3. POST-PROJECT PLANS Susteon demonstrated that its DAC technology has completed TRL 4: component and/or breadboard validation in a laboratory environment. The bench-scale testing of the sorbent coated filter confirmed the feasibility using the structured sorbent filter for DAC with joule-heated regeneration: 1. The sorbent can be coated and formed into the structured sorbent filter panel using commercially available filter manufacturing assembly lines. 2. The manufactured structured sorbent filter incorporating the ECCOsorb-T1 can be used for CO 2 removal from ambient air and Joule heated regeneration. Continuing TRL progression from TRL 4 to TRL 5 and beyond will require a multi-phase approach that includes further material and manufacturing improvements followed by a larger scale demonstration. Susteon’s plan focuses on parallel tracks of continued sorbent development and filter manufacturing improvements, integrated bench-scale system demonstration, and commercial de-risking to ensure a viable pathway to commercialization. The sorbent development will continue using Susteon’s lab-scale screening reactors and in-house synthesis expertise to improve performance metrics such as adsorption rate, CO capture capacity, and stability. 2 Successful iterations will be scaled up and integrated into the structured filter form factor and tested in Susteon’s 1-kg/day bench-scale system.
